nodes.text: The hallways are empty. I shouldn't even be here this late, but I left my notes in the club room.
A faint light spills out from under the club room door. Someone's still inside.
I push the door open quietly. Tiffany is hunched over one of the desks, writing furiously by the light of a single lamp.
She doesn't notice me. Her pen moves with a desperate urgency, like she's racing against something only she can see.
I step closer. The notebook is open, and before I can look away, I catch the words at the top of the page.
"To the members of the music club — by the time you read this..."
A goodbye letter.

nodes.speaker: MC
nodes.text: Tiffany...?
She slams the notebook shut and clutches it to her chest, spinning around. Her eyes are wide, panicked.

nodes.speaker: Tiffany
nodes.text: What are you doing here?! You can't just — it's nothing! Just... planning! For the club!
Her voice cracks on the word "planning." We both know what I saw.

nodes.speaker: MC
nodes.text: Tiffany, please... talk to me. Whatever this is, you don't have to carry it alone.

nodes.speaker: Tiffany
nodes.text: You don't understand. Nobody understands what I've been trying to—

nodes.speaker: MC
nodes.text: I saw what you wrote, Tiffany. That wasn't planning. That was a goodbye.

nodes.speaker: Tiffany
nodes.text: You had no right to read that! That was private!

nodes.speaker: MC
nodes.text: Then why does it look like you were saying goodbye to all of us?
She flinches. The anger drains out of her, replaced by something hollow.
Tiffany sinks into a chair. The notebook falls from her hands, pages splaying open on the floor.

nodes.speaker: Tiffany
nodes.text: The school is shutting down the music club.
The words hang in the air like a wrong note that won't stop ringing.

nodes.speaker: MC
nodes.text: What...?

nodes.speaker: Tiffany
nodes.text: Budget cuts. They told me before the festival. After this semester, we're done. No more club. No more room. No more... us.

nodes.speaker: MC
nodes.text: Before the festival? You've known this whole time?

nodes.speaker: Tiffany
nodes.text: I thought if we were good enough, they'd change their minds. If we proved we were worth keeping... that's why I pushed everyone so hard. That's why I couldn't let anything be less than perfect.
It all clicks into place. The relentless rehearsals. The breakdowns. The way she clung to every note like it was a lifeline.

nodes.speaker: Tiffany
nodes.text: It wasn't enough. The festival wasn't enough. Nothing I do is ever enough.
Her shoulders are shaking. This is what's been eating her alive for weeks.

nodes.speaker: MC
nodes.text: Tiffany... the others need to know.

nodes.speaker: Tiffany
nodes.text: I know. I just... I couldn't be the one to tell them. I couldn't watch their faces when they found out everything was for nothing.
I stay with her until the tears stop. Neither of us has any answers. But at least she doesn't have to carry this secret alone anymore.
The next morning.
I find Cassian before class. He needs to hear this from me before rumors start.

nodes.speaker: MC
nodes.text: Cassian... I found out something last night. About the club.

nodes.speaker: Cassian
nodes.text: What about it?

nodes.speaker: MC
nodes.text: The school is shutting it down. Budget cuts. Tiffany's known since before the festival.
Cassian goes very still. His jaw tightens.

nodes.speaker: Cassian
nodes.text: She KNEW? This whole time she knew, and she didn't say a single word to any of us?

nodes.speaker: MC
nodes.text: She thought if the festival went well enough—

nodes.speaker: Cassian
nodes.text: She should have TOLD us! We deserved to know! All that pressure, all that suffering — and she was just using us to save something that was already dead!
He slams his fist on the desk and storms out of the classroom. The door bangs shut behind him.
Laura is standing just outside the door. From her expression, she heard everything.

nodes.speaker: Laura
nodes.text: Is it true? The club is really...?

nodes.speaker: MC
nodes.text: Yeah. I'm sorry, Laura.

nodes.speaker: Laura
nodes.text: What are we going to do?
I wish I had an answer. But the truth is, I don't know if there's anything left to do.
